acceptance: The owner's chosen handling of a corpus difference on an automation adoption PR is implemented and documented in docs/internal/release-guide.md.

A test or dry run shows the chosen path on a release that changes a recorded output: either the automation lands it under the owner's rule, or it stops with a clear, owner-routed signal naming the changed cases (not a bare red CI job).
The ownership and trust checks in scripts/sqlglot_delivery.py are not weakened for anything except the corpus file, if the chosen option touches them.
context:
Decision gate: the owner chooses before implementation: (a) keep the corpus as a deliberate human gate, and make the delivery run report the changed cases to the owner (issue or summary) instead of leaving only a red job; (b) the delivery automation re-records the corpus inside its single adoption commit and lists the changed cases in the PR body, with a hold label so the owner approves before arming; (c) accept corpus changes automatically when the fork's real-engine tests passed for the delivered commit. Each changes how much of a release lands without a person; (c) removes an owner gate and needs explicit approval.

Verification rubric: (1) reproduce with the 30.33.0.1 delivery against a develop that still records the old BigQuery output; (2) the chosen path behaves as specified; (3) core workflow and delivery unit tests pass; (4) release-guide documents it.

Guardrails: no weakening of the adoption ownership checks beyond the corpus path; no change to the fork; the corpus stays owner-accepted by some explicit act; heavy runs through make heavy-run.

Owner decision 2026-11-17 (choice dialog): option (b) without the hold. The delivery prepare step re-records the golden corpus inside its single adoption commit and lists each changed case (before and after) in the PR body; the PR then takes the normal path (CI, execution evidence, review-gate, arm). The owner can stop it with no-auto-merge. The ownership check keeps its single-commit rule.
description: tests/unit/sql_compat/test_fork_golden_corpus.py compares legacy and fork SQL output with an owner-accepted recorded set. The delivery App's adoption pull request must carry exactly its one automation commit (scripts/sqlglot_delivery.py ownership check), so it cannot include a re-recorded corpus. Any upstream change that alters a recorded output therefore fails the adoption PR, and landing it needs a person to add a commit, which makes the PR human-owned and stops the automation arming it. This happened on 2026-11-17 with benchbox-sqlglot 30.33.0.1 (PR #4289): upstream d78ad66c changed BigQuery INFORMATION_SCHEMA quoting in bigquery_qualify_17/18. Upstream changes output often, so most releases may need a person, and sqlglot-e2e-first-release-certification can pass only on a release that changes no recorded output.
